title: CPUs, GPUs, TPUs & Apple silicon
summary: Understand accelerator families by their execution and memory models, not just their product names.
html:
Understand accelerator families by their execution and memory models, not just their product names.

CPU: flexible control and low latency

A CPU is good at irregular control flow, modest parallelism, orchestration, and many general-purpose tasks. Vector instructions accelerate arrays, while caches reduce repeated memory access. Small models or tiny batches may run efficiently on CPUs because accelerator launch and transfer overheads can dominate.

GPU: programmable parallel throughput

GPUs organize many lightweight threads around shared execution resources. NVIDIA exposes CUDA; AMD provides ROCm and HIP on supported devices; other platforms expose their own runtimes. Similar source syntax does not guarantee identical scheduling, numerical behavior, or kernel availability. Check the particular device and framework build.

TPU: matrix-centric execution

TPUs emphasize matrix multiplication and compiler-managed execution. Tensor layout, sharding, and compiler decisions matter greatly. Tensor programs must map to available operations and topology. A comparison with GPUs needs equal model quality, batch size, precision, memory fit, and software optimization effort.

Unified memory systems

Apple silicon integrates CPU and GPU with shared physical memory. This can avoid some explicit copies but does not eliminate synchronization or bandwidth limits. Metal provides GPU programming; frameworks such as MLX expose array operations on this architecture. Unified memory capacity is shared with the rest of the system.

Worked example

WorkloadFirst question
Interactive tiny modelDoes transfer or launch overhead dominate?
Large batched trainingCan matrix operations feed the accelerator efficiently?
Local LLMDo weights plus KV cache fit available memory?
Multi-device modelWhat is the interconnect and collective cost?

What goes wrong

A CUDA example does not run on Apple’s GPU simply because both devices are called GPUs. Portability is a software and kernel question as well as a hardware question.

Check your understanding

Does unified memory mean unlimited GPU memory?

Reveal the explanation

No. Physical capacity is finite and shared. The operating system and other applications also consume it.

How the pieces connect

A usable chapter has a flow of decisions, evidence, and checks. Use this diagram as a navigation aid, then test each step on a small real example.

An operating model for cpus, gpus, tpus & apple silicon

Accelerator choice is a workload and software decision. A theoretical peak describes a particular numerical operation under favorable conditions; it does not guarantee a specific model, framework, sequence length, or service will approach that peak. Memory capacity and a reliable kernel stack often matter more than the headline number.

The diagram is deliberately sequential, but real systems loop. A surprising result may expose a bad representation; a production incident may reveal a missing evaluation slice; a performance limit may require an algorithmic change. The point is to preserve the link between the abstract concept, the evidence you observe, and the decision you make next.

Field guide: four decisions in order

1. Characterize workload

Characterize workload establishes the next constraint. Measure shape, precision, batch, memory, and latency needs. Begin by making the object of study explicit. A vague input, target, or operating condition creates ambiguity that later computation cannot repair.

Write down the input boundary and the unit of analysis. This makes it possible to distinguish a missing fact from a mismatch between the question and the data or system.

2. Match hardware

Match hardware establishes the next constraint. Compare supported operations and memory model. Now make the mechanism inspectable. Prefer a small run whose intermediate values, examples, or traces can be examined before you automate a larger workflow.

Keep a concrete artifact: a small dataset, a notebook cell, a trace, a benchmark command, or a hand-worked calculation. It is the fastest way to surface hidden assumptions.

3. Map software

Map software establishes the next constraint. Validate framework, compiler, kernels, and libraries. Treat the first result as a measurement, not a conclusion. Compare it with a baseline and vary one assumption at a time so that the observed change has an interpretable cause.

Check a deliberately awkward case alongside the happy path. Boundary conditions, rare examples, and resource limits reveal more than another aggregate score.

4. Benchmark system

Benchmark system establishes the next constraint. Measure useful end-to-end throughput and tail latency. Finish by connecting the result to a real choice. Record the operating range, uncertainty, and the condition under which the next person should stop, escalate, or revisit the earlier steps.

Preserve the decision record with the result. A useful technical chapter leaves enough context for a reader to reproduce the reasoning, challenge it, and choose a safe next action.

When the first approach fails

Do not respond to a weak result by immediately adding scale, complexity, or another framework. First locate the failure: the input may not match the intended problem; the representation may discard a useful signal; the measurement may reward the wrong outcome; or the system may have crossed a memory, latency, reliability, or authority boundary. Change one layer, repeat the smallest useful check, and keep the before-and-after evidence.

Gotcha. A polished output can hide an untested assumption. The most convincing demonstration is a counterexample the workflow handles deliberately, with the limitation stated in the release or research record.

A rigorous way to practice

  1. Characterize workload. Measure shape, precision, batch, memory, and latency needs.
  2. Match hardware. Compare supported operations and memory model.
  3. Map software. Validate framework, compiler, kernels, and libraries.
  4. Benchmark system. Measure useful end-to-end throughput and tail latency.

Benchmark the exact model configuration with warmup, representative prompts or batches, and the required quality setting. Compare cost and energy per accepted task, not only tokens or FLOPS.

Questions that keep the chapter honest

AskWhy it mattersEvidence to collect
What assumptions does this method make?Every method encodes a view of data, hardware, or behavior.Inputs, representations, constraints, and cases outside the expected range.
What would make the result fail?Failure modes show where an aggregate result is fragile.Boundary cases, counterexamples, slices, and perturbations.
What decision changes if it improves?A metric only matters through an operational action.Baseline, threshold, cost, latency, and human-review consequences.
